brief: Dispersion trading, long single-stock vol against short index vol, has grown as clients seek correlation exposure. Two-way flow has increased, with clients also trading reverse dispersion (long correlation) after dispersion entry points hit all-time highs earlier in 2026. Goldman Sachs now offers an option on the implied dispersion level itself, excluding the realised component. Structure: an option tenor (e.g. 3m) sits on top of a dispersion package tenor (e.g. 1y) of forward-starting straddles on a fixed basket, struck at prevailing ATM spot on the option's maturity date. At maturity the option physically settles into the straddle package at the strike, though counterparties may instead agree to terminate at a price to mimic cash settlement. Buyer max loss is the premium paid; seller max loss is potentially unlimited. Because ATMF straddle premium is roughly linear in volatility, the package tracks the implied dispersion spread efficiently, and GS makes 2-way markets in both calls and puts. Worked example: a basket targeting $1m vega per leg prices a 1Y ATMS straddle package at $24,875,845 (24.4 vol-point spread); a 3m put struck 3 vol points lower costs $800,000 upfront (0.8 vol points).
